sequences.source_document: g22_W4312127096.xml.txt (publisher XML text), PDF for figures

steps.action: Proposed Local DA, a grid-independent LETKF-like scheme that can do hybrid and multiscale analysis without a large static ensemble.
steps.quote: it is desirable to design a flexible DA scheme that follows the grid-independent analysis of the LETKF

steps.action: Posed four issues: local hybrid and multiscale analysis, spatial continuity, impact of hybrid covariance and multiscale localization, and cycling performance. Also posed two LETKF comparison aims.
steps.quote: this study focuses on the following main issues: (i) how to locally conduct the hybrid and multiscale analysis

steps.action: Formulated the cost function on observed grid points and the explicit local correlation matrix C_oo with trace rescaling alpha. Thinned observations to keep the matrix size controllable.
steps.quote: We use a simple thinning approach to control the matrix size in this study, as described in the Appendix.

steps.action: In an early test (not shown), disabled thinning; Local DA became very time-consuming and analysis error rose because the uncorrelated observation-error assumption failed.
steps.quote: Our early test (not shown) indicates that Local DA becomes very time-consuming when the thinning process is disabled

steps.action: Chose a locally applied conjugate gradient solver, capped at 100 iterations, over matrix decomposition.
steps.quote: Local DA adopts an iterative algorithm, namely, the conjugate gradient (CG) method (Shewchuk, 1994)

steps.action: Checked the rank of the localized error-sample matrix (not shown): full rank in most cases, otherwise above 97 % of full rank.
steps.quote: Our early test (not shown) indicates that X ^ o is a full rank matrix in most cases.

steps.action: Adopted the Tang et al. (2014) linearization of nonlinear observation operators, which computes the observation prior from the ensemble-mean model state.
steps.quote: Local DA adopts the alternative approach proposed by Tang et al. (2014).

steps.action: Compared the chosen operator approximation against the ensemble mean of observation priors in an early test (not shown): reflectivity analysis error fell by about 2 dBZ.
steps.quote: Eq. (10) reduces the analysis error of reflectivity by approximately 2 dBZ in our early test (not shown).

steps.action: Built model-space multiscale localization (bandpass decomposition, per-scale radii, no cross-scale covariance), observation-space and double-space localization, the hybrid static/ensemble correlation, and the workflow.
steps.quote: We perform localization for each scale independently to construct the multiscale correlation matrix.

steps.action: Compared N-column with one-column analysis (not shown): slightly higher error, acceptable for N < 9, wall clock about 1/N. Five-column analysis was adopted.
steps.quote: the N -column analysis is slightly rasterized (not shown), leading to slightly higher errors than the one-column analysis

steps.action: Set the OSSE conditions with a WRF 5 km truth simulation of Typhoon In-fa (2021) initialized from GFS analysis.
steps.quote: The third typhoon of the 2021 western Pacific season, In-fa, is selected for the OSSEs performed herein.

steps.action: Checked the truth run against CMA observations of typhoon central pressure and location, following the Hoffman and Atlas (2016) OSSE criterion.
steps.quote: The simulated typhoon's central location also agrees with the CMA observation.

steps.action: Designed the test: a synthetic multiscale network (sounding, wind profiler, PWV, three radars) with perturbed observations, a 15-member time-lagged ensemble, 14 single-analysis configurations including LETKF, and three cycling experiments.
steps.quote: A total of 14 experiments for deterministic analyses at 00:00 UTC on 26 July 2021 are examined.

steps.action: Tested a 36-member ensemble, which gave lower analysis errors than the 15-member one (results not shown).
steps.quote: The authors have tested a larger ensemble with 36 members and obtained lower analysis errors than the 15-member counterpart.

steps.action: Mapped CG iteration counts and cost-function reduction across the domain for Hybrid_5band. Found slower convergence where observations are dense and no severe discontinuity between local analyses.
steps.quote: The results also indicate that no severe discontinuity occurs in Hybrid_5band, which is desired.

steps.action: Reran Hybrid_5band with radar data only and with a 500-iteration cap. This isolated radar data as the cause of non-convergence; all minimizations converged within 300 steps.
steps.quote: we rerun Hybrid_5band using only radar data and observe that only 4 % of all minimizations require more than 100 steps to converge

steps.action: Compared domain-averaged RMSE against truth for all configurations and the background (BAK), in observation space (Table 4) and model space (Table 5).
steps.quote: All experiments reduce the errors in the observation space after DA, but their differences are significant (Table 4).

steps.action: From the scale-decomposed hybrid results, proposed that restricting small-scale ensemble correlation to a small radius reduces analysis error.
steps.quote: constraining the small-scale ensemble correlation in a small radius may be conducive to the small analysis error

steps.action: Compared 2-, 3- and 5-band multiscale localization, with and without hybrid covariance, against Ens_noFLTR by scale (Fig. 8).
steps.quote: the small-scale analysis error becomes lower than that of Ens_noFLTR for all examined variables (Fig. 8)

steps.action: Kept the small-scale restriction assumption and judged three or five scales sufficient. Noted that qv error increased with more bands.
steps.quote: This result confirms the assumption that restricting the impact of small-scale correlation in a small region is beneficial.

steps.action: Compared double-space localization configurations by scale (Fig. 9) and by DTE maps at three levels (Fig. 10).
steps.quote: In contrast, Ens_noFLTR_DSL substantially reduces the analysis error of ps at all scales.

steps.action: Kept double-space localization as a supplement that reduces spurious small-scale increments.
steps.quote: double-space localization may serve as a supplement to pure model-space localization, which determines the level of analysis error

steps.action: Checked Local DA with observation-space localization against the LETKF on the same data, by scale-decomposed error (Fig. 11) and mu increment maps (Fig. 12). The analyses were similar.
steps.quote: Overall, in the case of using observation-space localization, Local DA can produce an analysis similar to the LETKF.

steps.action: Explained the higher qv error with more bands, and the scale dependence of gains, through the time-lagged ensemble's spread-RMSE relationship, rather than revising the small-scale restriction claim.
steps.quote: Therefore, it is not irrational for Ens_5band and Hybrid_5band to produce a higher analysis error for q v than Ens_2band.

steps.action: Compared hourly surface-pressure tendency in cycling experiments against the truth's balanced tendency (Fig. 15).
steps.quote: Hybrid_5band_DSL_6h produces a much smaller ps tendency than Ens_ noFLTR_6h

steps.action: Varied the cycling interval to 3 h. The ps tendency was not suppressed, which limited the cycling benefit to intervals long enough for spin-up.
steps.quote: When the cycling interval becomes shorter (Hybrid_5band_DSL_3h), the ps tendency cannot be effectively suppressed as Hybrid_5band_DSL_6h does.

steps.action: Compared the forecast and analysis RMSE evolution over cycles for u, v, qv and ps (Fig. 16), and maps of forecast error at 18:00 UTC (Fig. 17).
steps.quote: Ens_noFLTR_6h fails to decrease the forecast error after the second cycle, while Hybrid_5band_DSL_6h successively reduces the forecast and analysis error

steps.action: Kept the benefit of hybrid covariance with multiscale localization in cycling DA. Supported it with the evolution of ensemble spread versus RMSE (Fig. 18).
steps.quote: The above result confirms the benefit of using the hybrid covariance and multiscale localization.

steps.action: Characterized OpenMP parallel scaling from 1 to 32 cores (Fig. 19), run time (225 s on 16 cores), the share of cost by step, and memory use (about 4 GB, versus hundreds of MB for the LETKF).
steps.quote: the wall clock time is reduced by approximately 50 % upon doubling the number of cores

steps.action: Stated five conclusions: no severe discontinuity, affordable explicit matrix with thinning, hybrid gain, multiscale and double-space gains, and acceptable efficiency.
steps.quote: Local DA can effectively utilize the hybrid covariance to produce a better analysis than the analysis using ensemble covariance with a fixed localization radius.

steps.action: Restricted the double-space localization claim to noisy background covariance. Advised against it for well-sampled ensembles and for 4-D DA.
steps.quote: Despite the encouraging results, whether to use double-space localization should be considered case by case.

end.claim: In a perfect-model typhoon OSSE with a 15-member time-lagged ensemble, Local DA produces lower analysis error with hybrid covariance plus multiscale and double-space localization than with ensemble covariance at fixed radius. Its local CG solution shows no severe discontinuity, and its parallel efficiency is acceptable.

decisive_move.sentence: Comparing the RMSE against the known truth across the 14 configurations (Tables 4-5, then by scale in Figs. 7-9) is what turns the formulated scheme into a characterized capability.

gates.evidence: Action: the experiment set was directed by the features and comparison aims stated in §1 ¶11, not by a specific hypothesis. Claim: errors against a known truth could have shown no gain, and some configurations did fail (Ens_noFLTR_DSL in §4.2 ¶3; qv errors above BAK in §4.2.3 ¶1; the 3 h cycling run in §4.3.1 ¶3). Registration: localization radii were 'tuned for the case in which Typhoon In-fa made landfall' (§3.3.2 ¶1), and nothing was fixed before the data.

imports.item: Kalman filter framework underlying the LETKF (Hunt et al. 2007, Physica D)

novelty_claims.quote: [...] first paper to report on Local DA
Note that the LETKF of Wang et al. (2021) can also realize double-space localization, but this application has not yet been [...] .
it would be interesting to note the performance of the double-space localization approach, which has not yet been investigated
As the first study to present Local DA, this paper focuses on its idea and basic formulation.

limits: Evidence base: one simulated typhoon case in a perfect-model OSSE. There is no real-data test and no second case, so generalization is not shown. Several supporting checks are reported only as 'not shown': rank of the error-sample matrix, the observation-operator test, the N-column degradation, the 36-member ensemble, thinning disabled, and convective-area errors. Parameters were tuned on the same case, and the authors state many parameters are untested (§5 ¶2). The word 'significant' in §4.2 ¶1 is not backed by a statistical test. Cause unknown: the authors cannot explain why Static_BE and Hybrid_noFLTR are nearly identical (§4.2.1 ¶2). No review file or discussion was supplied, so no review sequence is coded. Sub-claims and their statuses: the LETKF similarity under observation-space localization is capability_characterized from one comparison; the small-scale restriction assumption is best_explanation, formed post hoc (steps 18-20) and protected by the spread argument (step 24); the cycling benefit is capability_characterized only for a 6 h interval. Inference: the label LDA_HBC_MSL in §4.4 ¶1 is not defined and probably denotes a hybrid multiscale configuration. Coding choices: the OSSE truth run is coded as F on mode hypothesis, following the codebook rule for set conditions, though it is a numerical experiment. capability_first fits only partly, since rival configurations were designed together with the method rather than after a phenomenon was established.

disagreements.target: Lei et al. (2021) EnKF-based hybrid scheme using a large (800-member) static ensemble
disagreements.support: The authors argue such large ensembles are often unaffordable and offer the explicit correlation matrix with a preset static correlation instead; they show hybrid gains with a 15-member ensemble.
disagreements.quote: The large ensemble ( > = 800 ) is not always available in practice because of the limited computational and storage resources.

disagreements.target: Common EnKF practice of approximating H from the departure of observation priors from their ensemble mean
disagreements.support: They follow Tang et al. (2014) and Yang et al. (2015) and report an early test (not shown) in which the alternative reduced reflectivity error by about 2 dBZ.
disagreements.quote: However, for nonlinear observation operators, there is an alternative, namely, the observation prior calculated using the ensemble mean of [...] .

alternatives_considered.alternatives: Ensemble control variable in a variational framework; averaging EnKF and variational analyses; large static ensemble (Lei et al. 2021)
alternatives_considered.reason: Explicitly constructed correlation matrix makes it straightforward; to evaluate the idea in a realistic scenario

alternatives_considered.alternatives: Square root of the background error covariance (variational practice)

alternatives_considered.reason: Better results in Tang et al. (2014) and Yang et al. (2015) for remote-sensing data

alternatives_considered.chosen: Bandpass as difference of two Gaussian low-pass analyses (Maddox 1980)
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Many ways to realize the bandpass filter

Cost control and uncorrelated observation errors
